overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance data clearly shows that astronomical 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies (especially regarding extreme planetary environments and planetary destruction concepts) dominate traction. Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieve high views-per-day and strong engagement (likes-per-view up to ~3.7%). Conversely, generic neuroscience facts and older static space facts show lower velocity.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) outperform standard descriptive space facts significantly within short timeframes.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-concept 'What If' immersion shorts focusing on extreme, visually striking space destinations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme temporal or physical anomalies like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (964 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,026 views) drive high sustained engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight mind-bending physical contrasts or extremes in the hook (e.g., planets, stars, or black holes breaking known laws).

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' stagnate around 10-70 views with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychology shorts unless paired with a high-stakes survival or sci-fi narrative framework.
